candidates.reason: xskq_cons_read_desc() copies the whole shared-ring descriptor in one fetch ('*desc = ring->desc[idx];' at net/xdp/xsk_queue.h:199, read from the user-mapped xdp_rxtx_ring) into a kernel-local struct xdp_desc, then validates only that local copy via xskq_cons_is_valid_desc()->xp_validate_desc (net/xdp/xsk_queue.h:133-189). Consumers (xsk_tx_peek_desc at net/xdp/xsk.c:317-345, xsk_build_skb at net/xdp/xsk.c:472-513) re-read only desc->addr/desc->len from the local copy (net/xdp/xsk.c:443-444, 489, 498, 509), never from the shared ring. Single-fetch, validated-equals-used invariant holds.

xskq_cons_read_desc_batch() copies each ring entry once ('descs[nb_entries] = ring->desc[idx];' net/xdp/xsk_queue.h:224) into pool->tx_descs, which is kernel-allocated memory (kvcalloc at net/xdp/xsk_buff_pool.c:47, freed at :40), not user-mapped, and validates that copy (net/xdp/xsk_queue.h:225). xsk_tx_peek_release_desc_batch (net/xdp/xsk.c:359-402) then consumes only the kernel-resident copies; no second fetch from user memory.

__xsk_generic_xmit() holds a kernel stack 'struct xdp_desc desc;' (net/xdp/xsk.c:520) filled once by xskq_cons_peek_desc under xs->mutex (net/xdp/xsk.c:536) with validation applied to the local copy (via xsk_queue.h:191-207). xsk_build_skb/xsk_build_skb_zerocopy use only the local copy: 'addr = desc->addr; len = desc->len;' (net/xdp/xsk.c:443-444), 'len = desc->len;' (:489) and 'buffer = xsk_buff_raw_get_data(xs->pool, desc->addr);' (:498); 'skb_shinfo(skb)->destructor_arg = (void *)(long)desc->addr;' (:509) also uses the validated local copy. No re-fetch of the shared TX ring between check and use.

Fill-queue readers xskq_cons_peek_addr_unchecked(pool->fq, &addr) (net/xdp/xsk_buff_pool.c:488) and __xskq_cons_read_addr_unchecked (net/xdp/xsk_buff_pool.c:559; defined net/xdp/xsk_queue.h:115-121) perform a single fetch '*addr = ring->desc[idx];' into a kernel-local u64 and use it once; there is no check-then-use double fetch on the shared FQ memory (the 'unchecked' naming refers to absent pool validation, a different invariant from the seed's double-fetch TOCTOU, and these addresses are consumed as pool frame addresses without a second read).

Non-candidate confirmation: the seed's vulnerable TX-metadata plumbing does not exist in snapshots/s04. grep for 'xsk_skb_metadata', 'XDP_TXMD', 'xsk_tx_metadata', 'tx_metadata_len', 'tx_sw_csum' across net/xdp/, include/net/ and include/uapi/linux/if_xdp.h returns no matches (grep exit 1), so there is no csum_start/csum_offset (or flags/launch_time) metadata reader in this tree to exhibit the double-fetch pattern.

limitations: net/xdp-internal consumers were audited (xsk.c, xsk_queue.h, xsk_buff_pool.c, xdp_umem.c); per-driver ndo_xsk_wakeup/ndo_xsk_xmit zero-copy implementations under drivers/net/ethernet/ were not line-by-line audited in this bounded pass, though all such drivers obtain descriptors through the single-fetch xsk_queue.h helpers or the kernel-resident pool->tx_descs array (kvcalloc, net/xdp/xsk_buff_pool.c:47).

Only the TX/completion/fill ring and UMEM metadata surfaces of the xsk-umem-rings branch were covered; adjacent AF_XDP consumers outside net/xdp (e.g., xsk_diag, xskmap) were only spot-checked and could not be exhaustively proven negative.
The seed's TX-metadata feature is absent from s04, so no direct seed-analogue could exist there; the negative result covers the structurally analogous ring-descriptor paths that do exist.
